prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Sign In to Access & Safeguard Your Saved Desktop Pets", "Log into your account to sync your existing pets, preserve customization details, and keep your virtual companions safe across sessions."]
1: ["Starter Companion"]
2: ["Preparing your desktop environment and loading pet render shaders..."]
3: ["Meet Your Virtual Desktop Companions", "Explore companion types before deciding whether to pick an instant pet or build a custom friend.", "Choose My Path"]
4: ["Pet Appearance & Asset Diagnostic", "We are verifying photo contours and texture rendering to ensure your pet generates correctly.", "Continue to Adoption"]
5: ["Clear Lighting Recommended"]
6: ["Initializing Desktop Pet Workspace", "Checking graphics acceleration and preparing desktop overlay windows..."]
7: ["Restore Your Existing Pet Companion", "Signing in connects your profile to your cloud-saved pets, ensuring seamless sync and preventing accidental pet resets."]
8: []
9: ["Official Desktop Companion"]
